oracleCaveats: This scenario's SAT verdict is only valid at bitwidth >= 8 (matching manifest.bitwidth and the hard-coded bitwidth:=8 in validate.cmd/query.cmd). At bitwidth 4-6, PropertyConfigurationVisitor's bitwidth-sufficiency check only validates declared Integer literal/attribute values, not Kodkod's internal encoding overhead for this scenario's 40-object self-referential relation with nested forAll -- so it silently returns a spurious near-instant UNSATISFIABLE with no warning (see constraints-and-configuration/config.bitwidth-insufficient-false-negative). If the harness is ever run at a lower bitwidth without updating this recorded expectation, the oracle would flip to a genuine false negative. The current SAT verdict itself is independently corroborated (check -v re-evaluation, a separate mv ? forAll query, and a graph-theoretic constructive 3-colorability proof), so this is a documented fragility to guard against, not a live concern.

supersession.kodkodReason: Spec S9 Study B case C: an invariant using OCL the Kodkod transformer drops silently. TypeConverter.convert has arms for Void, String/Boolean/Integer/Real, enums, classes, OclAny and collections, and NO arm for UReal, so a UReal attribute falls through to LOG.error(LogMessages.typeConvertError(...)) and return null (kk-modelvalidator TypeConverter.java:78). Observed on this exact model and section: 'ERROR org.tzi.use.kodkod.transform.TypeConverter - Cannot convert type UReal'. The null type means the attribute is never created on the incumbent's model, so the invariant that reads it fails to transform -- 'TransformationException: Cannot find attribute speed' thrown by VariableOperationVisitor.visitAttrOp -- and InvariantTransformator.transformAndAdd CATCHES that exception, logs it through printTransformationError, and then logs 'Invariant transformation successful' anyway (InvariantTransformator.java:129-166). What reaches the solver is class UnidentifiedObject with attributes=[] and invariants=[]: constant true, so TRIVIALLY_SATISFIABLE is returned with no search at all. UseKodkodModelValidator.trivially_satisfiable() then calls the SAME handleSolution() a real SATISFIABLE calls and builds an object diagram, so the incumbent does not merely fail to answer -- it presents an instance. The corpus run records that instance as 'UnidentifiedObject#count=1;UnidentifiedObject.objects=[UnidentifiedObject{speed=null}]': the very attribute the invariant constrains is absent from the snapshot offered as a witness. Nothing warns. Observed for this section: PropertyConfigurationVisitor.containErrors() is false and its warning writer receives the EMPTY string, and the benchmark's own results row for DefaultSAT4J carries error=null. The one log4j ERROR line above never reaches the outcome, the object diagram, or the corpus log -- which is what 'silently' means here.
supersession.groundTruth: UNSATISFIABLE. The configuration pins the search space to exactly one object (UnidentifiedObject_min = UnidentifiedObject_max = 1) and exactly one candidate attribute value (UnidentifiedObject_speed_value = Set{0.3328970694541931152343750}, UnidentifiedObject_speed_uncertainty = Set{0.02}), so the entire space is a single snapshot. USE's own evaluator -- neither model finder -- evaluates UnidentifiedObject::ReliablyFast FALSE on that snapshot, because (self.speed > 0.30) carries confidence 0.9499999997475513, just under the 0.95 the invariant demands. One candidate, and it fails, so no satisfying instance exists. A reader re-establishes this with the USE evaluator alone; SupersessionDivergenceTest.useEvaluatorRefutesTheSingleCandidateEachConfigurationAllows does exactly that, from the corpus files, with no solver involved.

oracleCaveats: The recorded expectation is the SMT-Z3 answer. The incumbent's cell for this row is TRIVIALLY_SATISFIABLE and is WRONG, not a second opinion -- see the supersession block.

The divergence is classified false-sat, the strong claim, and it is the DANGEROUS direction: the incumbent reports a satisfying instance for a model that has none. A false-unsat row (IntegerBitwidth-DailyCap, RealGrid-UnitInterval) is a visible failure to produce a snapshot; this one is a snapshot a user has no reason to distrust.

The margin is deliberately a hair: 0.9499999997475513 against a 0.95 threshold. That makes the row a boundary case for the SMT finder's own precision, and it is NOT what earns the false-sat label -- the incumbent never evaluates the threshold at all, since the invariant is gone before the solver runs. URealThreshold-NominalErasure carries the same claim with a wide margin (0.69146 against 0.95) for exactly that reason.

The mechanism is shared with URealThreshold-NominalErasure and with the At/Above rows, which are not Study B rows because their ground truth is SATISFIABLE: the incumbent's TRIVIALLY_SATISFIABLE happens to point the same way there, so those rows evidence the drop without evidencing a wrong answer.

supersession.kodkodReason: Spec S9 Study B case D: a U-typed model the incumbent cannot configure at all.
